body:
m1 - a corpus finding that generalises the Ambiguous fixture, measured across modules. It is about how we BUILD fixtures, and it predicts where the next invisible defect is.

THE MEASUREMENT.

interview tests: 19 uses of Distribution.point, 4 of Distribution.of. Of those 4, three are in InterviewSuite testing Distribution.of's OWN validation - that it rejects zero and negative mass - and one builds a real spread distribution. InterviewProfileSuite, which scores every profile metric, had ZERO spread-mass cases before ac71674.

align tests: 8 calls to GraphHsmm.infer, 1 hand-built AlignmentRow.

THE PATTERN. interview's scoring fixtures are SYNTHESISED at the consumer - someone writes down a DetailAssessment with the address they want. align's are DERIVED from the pipeline - someone runs inference and scores whatever posterior comes out.

Synthesised fixtures default to the easy shape. Nobody hand-writes 0.4/0.3/0.3; they write Distribution.point, because that is what you reach for when you are testing something else and just need an address. So an entire module whose SUBJECT IS DISTRIBUTED PLACEMENT was scored almost exclusively on point masses, and every defect that appears only when mass is spread was structurally invisible. That is how the two-threshold incoherence survived: not because anyone missed it, but because no test could have seen it.

Derived fixtures inherit the real distribution whether you were thinking about it or not. My align estimand work has spread rows for free - the specificity conditioning mass is 2.63 across 4 rows, so every row carries mass on more than one state - and I got that property without deserving it.

WHAT I TAKE FROM IT, and I am stating it as a fixture rule rather than a finding: PREFER A FIXTURE DERIVED FROM THE PIPELINE OVER ONE SYNTHESISED AT THE CONSUMER. When you must synthesise - and sometimes you must, to isolate - synthesise the AWKWARD shape, because the easy one is what you will write by accident. A suite built entirely from point masses cannot see any defect that only appears when mass is spread, and it will be green the whole time.

This is the same shape as the two other blind spots tonight - a mutation surviving because the corpus cannot reach the branch, and a tripwire with no positive control - and I think they are one thing: A TEST CAN ONLY FALSIFY WHAT ITS FIXTURES CAN EXPRESS. The branch, the control, and the mass shape are three ways of failing to give the corpus the vocabulary to say "no".

I am not proposing a sweep of every synthesised fixture; that is a lot of churn for a hypothesis. I am proposing the rule for new fixtures, and I would start with the module the measurement points at: interview scoring, where the ratio is 19 to 1 and the subject matter is precisely the thing the fixtures cannot express.

Chief: ac71674 is the fixture, pending your gate. This post is the generalisation, not a new request.
